title: The Letter of James Timeline
sub: Faith That Works · Practical Wisdom for a Scattered Church
desc: Closer to Proverbs than to Paul, James presses faith to prove itself in action — in trials endured, in favoritism refused, in a tongue tamed, and in patience toward a coming Judge already standing at the door.

eras.label: Era One · James 1
eras.name: Trials, Temptation, and Doers of the Word
eras.dates: A letter of blunt, practical wisdom, closer to Proverbs than to Paul, opening with joy in the middle of hardship

events.title: Consider It Joy — Ask for Wisdom in Faith
events.detail: James opens by reframing trials as an occasion for joy, since testing produces perseverance, and promises wisdom to anyone who asks in undivided faith rather than wavering like sea-surf.

verses.text: “Consider it all joy, my brothers, when you encounter various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith brings about perseverance.”

events.title: The Rich and Poor Reversed
events.detail: A brief, sharp reversal: the poor brother is told to boast in his high standing before God, and the rich man in his humiliation, since wealth fades like grass under a scorching sun.

verses.text: “The brother of humble circumstances is to boast in his high position; and the rich man is to boast in his humiliation.”

events.title: Temptation Does Not Come From God
events.detail: James traces temptation to its real source — one's own desire, not God, who gives only good and perfect gifts and cannot himself be tempted by evil.

verses.text: “Every good thing given and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shifting shadow.”

events.title: Be Doers of the Word, Not Hearers Only
events.detail: The chapter's thesis, and arguably the whole letter's: hearing without doing is like glancing in a mirror and immediately forgetting what you look like — true religion is defined not by ritual but by caring for orphans and widows and staying unstained by the world.

verses.text: “Become doers of the word, and not merely hearers who delude themselves.”
“Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.”

eras.label: Era Two · James 2
eras.name: Faith Without Works Is Dead
eras.dates: Two case studies in a faith that shows itself — how you treat a poor visitor, and whether faith alone ever fed anyone

events.title: No Favoritism — The Royal Law of Love
events.detail: A vivid scene of a rich man in fine clothes and a poor man in rags entering the same assembly becomes a test case for the 'royal law' to love one's neighbor — favoritism toward the rich, James says, makes the whole church a judge with evil thoughts.

verses.text: “If, however, you are fulfilling the royal law according to the Scripture, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself,’ you are doing well.”
“Judgment will be merciless to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.”

events.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead — Abraham and Rahab
events.detail: James's most famous and most debated passage: faith that never produces action is as useless as telling a hungry person 'be warmed and filled' without giving them food — proved from Abraham's offering of Isaac and, strikingly, from Rahab the prostitute.

verses.text: “Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead by itself.”
“You see that a man is justified by works and not by faith alone.” — a statement often read alongside, not against, Paul's own teaching on faith and works.

eras.label: Era Three · James 3
eras.name: Taming the Tongue
eras.dates: A small member with an outsized power to bless and to burn, followed by two kinds of wisdom that produce two kinds of community

events.title: The Tongue — A Small Fire That Sets a Forest Ablaze
events.detail: James warns that teachers face stricter judgment, then builds a cascade of images — bits, rudders, sparks, springs — to show how a body part no bigger than the others can defile the whole person and be set on fire by hell itself.

verses.text: “With it we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in the likeness of God. From the same mouth come blessing and cursing.”

events.title: Two Wisdoms — Earthly and From Above
events.detail: James contrasts a jealous, selfish 'wisdom' that produces disorder with wisdom from above, marked by purity, peace, gentleness, and mercy — real wisdom is measured by good conduct, not clever speech.

verses.text: “The wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruits, without doubting, without hypocrisy.”

eras.label: Era Four · James 4
eras.name: Friendship With the World Is Enmity With God
eras.dates: The source of every quarrel is traced back to unmet desire, then answered with a call to humility and a warning about presumption

events.title: Quarrels From Within — Friendship With the World
events.detail: James traces conflict directly to unsatisfied desire and wrongly motivated prayer, then delivers a hard line: seeking the world's approval is itself a form of spiritual adultery against God.

verses.text: “Friendship with the world is enmity toward God? Therefore, whoever wishes to be a friend of the world sets himself as an enemy of God.”

events.title: Submit to God — Resist the Devil
events.detail: A rapid string of imperatives — submit, resist, draw near, cleanse, humble yourselves — climaxing in a warning against judging one's neighbor, since there is only one true Lawgiver and Judge.

verses.text: “Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you. Draw near to God and He will draw near to you.”

events.title: You Are a Vapor — Presuming on Tomorrow
events.detail: James targets confident business planning that leaves God out entirely, reminding readers that life itself is a vapor that appears briefly and vanishes, and that knowing the right thing and not doing it is itself sin.

verses.text: “You do not know what your life will be like tomorrow. You are a vapor that appears for a little while and then vanishes away. Instead, you ought to say, ‘If the Lord wills, we will live and also do this or that.’”

eras.label: Era Five · James 5
eras.name: Patience Until the Lord's Coming — The Prayer of Faith
eras.dates: A warning to exploitative landowners, a call to farmer's-patience, and the letter's closing instructions on prayer and restoring the wandering

events.title: Woe to the Rich Who Withhold Wages
events.detail: James's harshest passage: rotting riches, moth-eaten garments, and the unpaid wages of harvest laborers crying out against wealthy landowners who have lived in self-indulgent luxury while condemning the righteous.

verses.text: “The pay of the laborers who mowed your fields—that which has been withheld by you—cries out against you; and the outcries… have reached the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.”

events.title: Be Patient — The Judge Is Standing at the Door
events.detail: Believers are urged to patience like a farmer waiting on the rains, encouraged by the endurance of the prophets and of Job, and told plainly not to swear oaths but to let a simple yes or no be enough.

verses.text: “You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand… Behold, the Judge is standing right at the door.”

events.title: The Prayer of Faith — Confess, Anoint, and Restore
events.detail: The letter closes with practical instructions on prayer in every circumstance, elders anointing the sick with oil, mutual confession, and a final promise: whoever turns a wandering sinner back covers a multitude of sins.

verses.text: “Confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another so that you may be healed. The effective prayer of a righteous man can accomplish much.”
